_comment: Each entry pairs a bug that reached production with the test that must catch it.
verify-guards.sh applies the mutation, runs only the named test file, and
requires it to FAIL. A guard that still passes under mutation is not a guard.
'find' must match exactly once. If it stops matching, the guarded code has
changed and the job fails as STALE -- distinctly from a guard failure, because
the two need different responses: stale means re-verify the guard still covers
the bug; failure means the guard has stopped working.

mutations.bug: ACP checkout returned 404 on every route; the /acp prefix was not stripped before dispatch (#62)
Eight routes unreachable in production, including all health/metrics and the /v1/orgs family (#69)
POST /v1/analyze raised for every authenticated caller; the ETS table was created in Plug init/1, which runs at compile time (#91)
mutations.find:
# Belt and braces: rate limiting must never be the reason an analysis fails.
    init_table()

mutations.bug: Every completed Pro checkout ended on a 500; get_session/2 was called without fetching the session (#90)
Unauthenticated signup issued an admin-scoped key for an existing org when the name matched (#89)
ACP endpoints had no rate limiting; an unauthenticated caller could create unbounded sessions, orgs and API keys

Anticipated, not yet shipped: a replayed Stripe webhook or resubmitted x402 payment proof double-credits an org. The defence is the unique index on external_ref, surfaced through the changeset constraint -- without it a duplicate raises Ecto.ConstraintError instead of returning {:error, :duplicate}, which callers will not be expecting.

A failed scan left the BEAM's working directory inside a checkout that was then deleted. cwd is node-global, so every later relative path failed with 'could not get current working directory'. Surfaced as an order-dependent cascade in CI that the test retry loop had been hiding (#108).
mutations.find:
try do
      File.cd!(path)
      fun.()
    after
      File.cd!(cwd)
    end

mutations.bug: GET /url= hung forever in production. find_binary_files shelled out to `grep -rIL .` with no file operand: GNU grep searches the working directory, BusyBox grep -- what the Alpine runtime image provides -- reads stdin, and System.cmd holds the child's stdin open forever. No assertion about grep's behaviour can catch this on a machine with GNU grep, so the guard is the absence of the external process: the test runs with PATH emptied.
mutations.replace: |> Stream.filter(fn f -> match?({_, 0}, System.cmd("grep", ["-qI", ".", f])) end)

mutations.bug: A wrong STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET failed identically to an unset one and to a scanner POSTing junk -- all three returned 400 with no way to tell them apart. The secret sat set-but-wrong with webhooks silently 400ing and nothing surfaced it. Collapsing 'unconfigured' back into 'invalid' makes the monitor report a rotation problem when the real fault is a missing secret.

The usage row and its ledger debit are one transaction because they describe the same event: a committed usage row with no debit is an analysis delivered and never accounted for, findable only by reconciliation after the fact. Letting a failed debit fall through instead of rolling back recreates that gap on every failure.
Anticipated: dropping the ledger debit from the usage path leaves analyses consumed with no internal record of what they cost, which is the state ADR-002 exists to end.

A wallet address is public, so provisioning that returns an existing org for a presented address hands an attacker a credential for someone else's funded org -- #89's bug in a new costume. provision/2 must never return an existing org; only the caller, having proved control, may decide that.

A wallet costs nothing to create, so any per-wallet free allowance is a per-attacker free allowance. Giving wallet orgs the default free-tier limit reopens the farming vector ADR-002 closes by granting none.

A wallet org's only gate is its credit balance, checked before the analysis runs. Falling through to the tier check would serve a zero-balance agent for free, and ADR-002 allows balances to go negative precisely because refusal has to happen before the work.
mutations.find:
%Org{wallet_address: wallet} = org when is_binary(wallet) and wallet != "" ->
        check_credit_balance(org)

mutations.bug: The first version inferred the ledger's start date from the earliest credit entry, so an empty ledger made every usage row 'pre-ledger' and the check reported clean having reconciled nothing -- a check that passes by examining nothing, which is the failure it exists to catch. The start now comes from when the credit_entries migration ran, and an unknown start excludes nothing rather than everything.
A balance is money. /v1/credits derives org_id from the authenticated API key and nothing else; taking it from a query parameter would let any key read any org's ledger.
